scope: Health-only scenario for a proposed additional SF employment place; not education, other cities, or total economic-mobility value.

judgments.label: Additional place budget
judgments.basis: Assumed nominal $20,000 all-in allowance for six months of paid internship wages, casework, training, supervision and overhead. $12,000–$30,000 stress cases are not quotes. Neither one public grant divided by participants nor whole-program expenses across mismatched years supplies the marginal cost.

judgments.label: Incremental health utility
judgments.basis: Subjective .005: a small health gain, one-quarter of a .02 endpoint reference from England's health-selected adult IPS trial. This is calibration, not a transferred causal coefficient. Youth internships differ substantially; JOBS II found no mean EQ-5D benefit.

judgments.label: Effective benefit duration
judgments.basis: Half an equivalent full-effect year within a one-year horizon, allowing gradual emergence/fading. Not .005 measured accumulated QALYs or a lifetime assumption.

judgments.label: Additional engagement multiplier
judgments.basis: Set1: the subjective local health gain is already averaged across the offered-place cohort including unsuccessful engagement. No second completion or employment-rate multiplier.

judgments.label: New funded capacity
judgments.basis: 50% judgment for new places versus replacement of existing public/private commitments. Actual donor tranche and capacity unknown.

nullBoundary: No added effective support or no health benefit means no finite positive-benefit price. Harm remains possible; the model preserves signed utility. Positive scenarios are judgments, not confidence bounds. This health-only lens omits the program's principal economic-mobility benefits.

fundingRoom.nextEvidence: A six-month SF cohort quote, all-funder cost ledger, actual additional slots, consistent dosage, and complete health/employment outcomes against ordinary alternatives.

excluded: Wages and earnings converted into QALYs
Deaths prevented borrowed from unrelated youth jobs trials
Confidence scores treated as health utility
Education, housing and future benefits beyond the narrow one-year health horizon
